To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the number of papers published in the most important international mammalian journals on the conservation of threatened species increased from 2001 to 2011; 2) the number of threatened species considered in the papers published in the four journals increased during this decade, but the proportion of threatened species in the papers published each year remained constant, suggesting that the conservation research effort is not being directed towards threatened species;

(1) the orders that receive the most attention are not the ones with the highest percentage of threatened species, and (2) the Nearctic and Pa-leartic Regions receive more attention than expected, while the Oriental Region receives less attention than expected.
